mfa_enforced_at_boundary_crossing.title: MFA Enforced at Boundary Crossing
mfa_enforced_at_boundary_crossing.description: Attests that every remote-access session crossing this boundary (VPN tunnel, bastion login, ZTNA grant) requires multi-factor authentication before the session is established — no password-only path, no bypass groups, no single-factor fallback. True when MFA is uniformly enforced at the crossing; false when the boundary accepts single-factor (password-only) authentication.

phishing_resistant_authenticator_require.title: Phishing-Resistant Authenticator Required
phishing_resistant_authenticator_require.description: Attestation: the remote-access boundary (VPN/bastion/ZTNA portal) accepts ONLY phishing-resistant authenticators — FIDO2/WebAuthn security keys or PKI smartcards (PIV/CAC) — for the second factor. SMS, voice, email OTP, and push-only methods are disabled for this app. Fires (insecure) when phishable factors are permitted, allowing an adversary-in-the-middle proxy to relay credentials and OTP/push approval in real time. Source: CISA Implementing Phishing-Resistant MFA fact sheet; NSA/CISA Selecting and Hardening Standards-based Remote Access VPN Solutions.

vpn_protocol_modern_strong.title: VPN Protocol Modern and Strong
vpn_protocol_modern_strong.description: Attestation: the remote-access tunnel negotiates only a modern, NIST-recommended VPN protocol — WireGuard, IKEv2/IPsec with strong suites, or TLS-based SSL VPN with current TLS (>=1.2, preferably 1.3). Legacy protocols (PPTP, bare L2TP without IPsec, IKEv1 aggressive-mode PSK, SSLv2/SSLv3) are disabled on the concentrator and not negotiable. Interpreted boolean (not a substring of a protocol-list string) so polarity is safe: the secure attestation is true, the insecure attestation (legacy protocol enabled or negotiable) is false. Grounded in NIST SP 800-77r1 (IPsec) and NIST SP 800-113 (SSL VPN); operationalised by NSA/CISA Selecting and Hardening Standards-based Remote Access VPN Solutions.

vpn_cipher_suites_strong_only.title: VPN Cipher Suites Strong Only
vpn_cipher_suites_strong_only.description: Attestation: the tunnel's negotiable cryptographic proposals include only NIST-approved suites for key exchange, encryption, and integrity — e.g. ECDH P-256+ or X25519 for KEX, AES-GCM-128/256 for confidentiality, SHA-256+ for integrity. Weak/legacy primitives (DES, 3DES, RC4, MD5, SHA-1, anon-DH, export-grade, CBC-mode in SSH contexts) are absent from IKE/IPsec proposals, openvpn cipher/tls-cipher lists, and TLS suite lists. Modeled as an interpreted boolean rather than a regex over the raw cipher string because raw cipher lists are composite directives where 'HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5' securely excludes weak tokens that still appear as substrings — pattern matching would false-fire on hardened config. The assessor interprets the raw configuration (per the dossier inspect commands: testssl.sh, ike-scan -M, sshd -T ciphers/macs/kex) and attests true when only strong suites are negotiable. Grounded in NIST SP 800-77r1 and NIST SP 800-113.

split_tunnel_disabled.title: Split Tunnel Disabled
split_tunnel_disabled.description: Interpreted attestation: the remote-access channel forces ALL client traffic — including DNS — through the VPN tunnel (full-tunnel mode, default route 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 pushed, corporate DNS pushed, no split-include/exclude routes for internet ranges). True iff there is no parallel cleartext egress path on the VPN-connected device that could bridge untrusted-to-trusted. Per NSA/CISA Selecting and Hardening Standards-based Remote Access VPN Solutions and CMMC SC.L2-3.13.7.

admin_endpoint_health_attested_at_elevat.title: Admin Endpoint Health Attested at Elevation
admin_endpoint_health_attested_at_elevat.description: Attestation: before the remote-access session (VPN tunnel, bastion login, ZTNA grant) is established, the policy enforcement point evaluates endpoint health signals — patch level, EDR/AV running and healthy, disk encryption on, OS within supported baseline — as a hard precondition; non-compliant devices are denied or quarantined. True means a device-trust posture verdict gates admission; false means admission is granted on user credentials alone.

managed_device_enrollment_enforced.title: Managed Device Enrollment Enforced
managed_device_enrollment_enforced.description: Attestation: the remote-access boundary requires a managed-device claim (MDM/UEM enrollment, corporate device certificate, or equivalent attested device identity) before granting the tunnel/session; unenrolled or BYOD devices without a verified managed identity are refused. True means only enrolled/managed devices may cross the boundary; false means any device with valid user credentials is admitted.

bastion_mediates_all_admin_access.title: Bastion Mediates All Admin Access
bastion_mediates_all_admin_access.description: Attestation: administrative SSH/RDP into the trusted zone is mediated exclusively through the bastion / jump host — production hosts reject management connections from any non-bastion source via host firewall and network ACL, and no direct admin path bypasses recording / JIT / mediation controls. Verified by attempting ssh/rdp to a production management interface from a non-bastion user-network source (must be refused/filtered) and by reviewing network ACLs / security groups so inbound 22/3389 (and equivalent management ports) is restricted to the bastion's source identity with no broader allow-list.

no_standing_admin_privileges_jit_require.title: No Standing Admin Privileges — JIT Required
no_standing_admin_privileges_jit_require.description: Attests that administrative privilege on production is granted just-in-time (time-bound, approval-gated) and that no permanent/standing admin entitlements exist on production hosts or control-plane roles. Secure value is true (JIT-only, no standing admin); insecure value is false (standing admin entitlements present). When false, an attacker who compromises a user account inherits durable admin power without traversing a recorded, gated path.

privileged_access_via_pam_with_session_r.title: Privileged Access via PAM with Session Recording
privileged_access_via_pam_with_session_r.description: Attests that all interactive administrative sessions traverse a PAM/bastion that records the session (keystroke, command transcript, or video) to tamper-evident storage. Secure value is true (PAM-mediated and recorded); insecure value is false (no bastion/PAM mediation or no session recording). When false, admin actions are unattributable and forensically opaque, removing the deterrent and detection value of mediation.

edge_appliance_patched_within_sla.title: Edge Appliance Patched Within SLA
edge_appliance_patched_within_sla.description: Attests the VPN/bastion edge appliance is on a vendor-supported version and current on security patches within the organisation's SLA, with no open KEV-listed CVE applicable to the running version. True when the running version is supported and not affected by any open KEV entry; false when the appliance is end-of-support, behind on critical patches, or exposed to a publicly-known unpatched CVE (e.g. CVE-2023-27997 FortiOS, CVE-2024-3400 PAN-OS, CVE-2023-46805 Ivanti Connect Secure).

edge_management_interfaces_not_internet_.title: Edge Management Interfaces Not Internet-Reachable
edge_management_interfaces_not_internet_.description: Attests the VPN/bastion edge appliance's administrative / management interfaces (web-admin, SSH-admin, API console on ports such as 8443/4443/22) are not reachable from untrusted internet sources — only the VPN service ports answer on the public interface; the management plane is bound to an internal interface or jump-host network. True when an internet-side port scan returns only sanctioned VPN service ports; false when admin/management interfaces are exposed publicly.
